statement: A recent, specific summary of a process reads as sufficient authority precisely because it is recent and specific, while the document that defines the process is older and longer and gets skipped. But a summary omits invocation context -- who calls this, with what arguments, at which point -- which is exactly what a caller needs. Cutting 0.4.9 I built the post-tag sequence from a handover brief rather than from docs/release-process.md, which the brief itself cited as authoritative, and handed the operator three commands that could not work: verify-release-currency.mjs, verify-cejel-release-set.mjs and verify-mcp-oci-release-chain.mjs are each a step inside a workflow_dispatch workflow that computes their arguments, not standalone commands. Two refused with usage lines; the third fails by construction before publishing, because it checks published surfaces. Three round trips. Read the source a summary cites before issuing commands derived from the summary.

movesWhen.reason: This is a release-review practice: each future command set must be derived from the authoritative process document in its actual invocation context. The repository already has docs/release-process.md; no single corrective commit can prove that future handovers will read it rather than a summary.

statement: Every defect found in one day's work on this repository had the same shape: the control existed somewhere no mechanism reads. The cycle-13 measurement freeze lived in a signed record in another repository and in one pull-request comment, while branch protection required two checks that knew nothing about a window. docs/calibration/ was treated as an authority path though the repository shipped no allowed-signers file and no check read a signature: of every commit that had ever touched it, five were unsigned and three signed by a key the repository does not list, none verifiable. A pre-commit hook refusing commits on main existed untracked on one machine, so no fresh clone and no agent worktree ever ran it. Ask of any control: what reads it, and what happens when nothing does. A rule whose only reader is a person is a habit, not a control.

movesWhen.reason: The documented gap remains open: no tracked mechanism verifies core.hooksPath for fresh clones or worktrees, and no automated reader verifies the reviewer half of this control. A future Cejel guard must establish both readers before this lesson can anchor to its landed fix.
